About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About the NPI Team

The New Product Introduction (NPI) team moves hardware design changes and brand-new products from concept development through large-scale production and commercial use. We coordinate across design, testing, supply chain, quality, manufacturing, and field operations to ensure products are ready to build, launch, and scale in support of Zipline’s mission.

About The Role

This role on the Change Management/NPI team will help us level up our ability to process and implement changes at high volume and high change velocity. Zipline’s unique ability to quickly improve our hardware and develop new designs allowed us to launch our hardware so successfully, and this role with unlock our ability to expand across the United States and beyond while maintaining the same design improvement velocity.

What You'll Do

- Build a tool that visualizes hardware changes over time, shows how product configurations evolve, and highlights hardware capabilities at specified timestamps.

- Build a tool that evaluates configuration compatibility across current and previous hardware revisions and summarizes hardware capabilities for specified configurations.

- Build a user interface for submitting engineering changes that standardizes required information, reduces errors, and generates complete change summaries for technical and non-technical audiences.

What You'll Bring

- Currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, computer science, information systems, data science, or a related technical field.

- Demonstrated experience through coursework, personal projects, research, student organizations, or prior internships building software, data, dashboard, or automation tools.

- Familiarity with at least one technical tool or language used to build solutions, such as Python, JavaScript, SQL, APIs, spreadsheets, databases, or low-code application platforms.

- Strong analytical and systems-thinking skills, with the ability to understand relationships, dependencies, and business rules within complex, multi-level assemblies or product data.

- Ability to gather requirements from users, ask clarifying questions, and turn ambiguous problems into clear workflows, visualizations, or user-friendly interfaces.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document information, explain technical outputs to non-technical audiences, and incorporate feedback from technical and non-technical stakeholders.

- Detail-oriented and organized, with the ability to validate data, manage changing priorities, and work independently and collaboratively on complex projects.

What Else You Should Know

This internship is a full-time position, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Spring 2027 interns from January to April. Zipline is unable to sponsor work visas for applicants to this position.

Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements.

Candidates are limited to three (3) applications within a 30-day period.

Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities.

Zipline is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your point of contact at Zipline know if you require any accommodations throughout your interview process.

Voluntary Self-Identification

The job:
As a Data Engineering Intern, you'll spend the summer building the datasets and pipelines that teams across Buildertrend rely on to make decisions. You'll work alongside experienced data engineers, get hands-on with a modern data stack, and learn how raw data from tools like Salesforce and SQL Server becomes curated, trustworthy datasets that power our BI, analytics and AI initiatives. We don't expect you to already know every framework we use. We're looking for curiosity, solid fundamentals and a real interest in the craft of data engineering. By the end of the internship, you'll have sharpened your technical skills, gained real engineering experience and shipped work that helps the business run on numbers people can trust.

What you will do:

- Help build and maintain ELT/ETL pipelines that bring data in from sources like SQL Server, Salesforce and other business tools, and turn it into clean, usable datasets.

- Write SQL to transform, model and prepare data that supports BI, product analytics, and ML/AI use cases.

- Partner with Data Engineers, Analysts and other stakeholders to understand what a dataset needs to do before you build it.

- Learn our modern data stack, including Databricks, dbt and a medallion (bronze, silver, gold) approach to organizing data, with guidance and mentorship along the way.

- Write and run data quality and freshness checks so the teams using your datasets can trust the numbers.

- Document what you build, including table definitions, column notes and simple diagrams, clearly enough for both people and AI tools to use.

- Use AI-assisted development tools, including Claude, to accelerate coding, debugging and problem-solving workflows while still being responsible and accountable for the quality and accuracy of your work.

- Complete assigned tasks and projects within established sprint timelines.

Who you are and what you need:

- Currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree in computer science, data science, or a related field.

- Available to work full-time onsite at the Buildertrend HQ in Omaha, NE, for the full summer.

- Strong interest in data engineering, including building datasets, ETL/ELT, and getting data ready to support BI, analytics and ML/AI work.

- Familiar with SQL and at least one programming language such as Python (through coursework or personal projects is perfectly fine).

- Curiosity about data tools and frameworks like Databricks and dbt, and an eagerness to learn them on the job.

- Experience using AI tools (such as Claude, GitHub Copilot or similar) in coursework or personal projects, or a strong interest in learning how to use them effectively.

- Strong problem-solving and analytical skills, and comfort working with data.

- Clear and effective written and verbal communication skills.

- Comfortable working independently and as part of a team.

- Eager to learn, ask questions and apply feedback constructively.

We are giving you:

- Office environment with all the perks of a high-energy tech company.

- Free daily lunches at the office.

- Summer housing at a local university – you can skip the summer housing search and focus on the experience.

- Onsite fitness center to keep you feeling your best.

- No weekend hours – just work hard Monday-Friday between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m.

- Monthly events to connect other interns and Buildertrend employees.

Who we are:

Great builders don’t just manage projects – they run successful businesses. That’s where Buildertrend comes in. As the leading residential construction management platform, we give contractors the power to control their financials, schedules, team workflows and client relationships – all in one system. No more juggling disconnected tools or guessing on profitability. With nearly two decades of industry expertise, Buildertrend helps builders work smarter, scale faster and stay ahead of the competition. If you want to learn more about us, check out: https://buildertrend.com/about/

SkillBridge Program Description:

As one of the largest global security companies in the world, Northrop Grumman is proud to help our nation’s military personnel navigate their next chapter into civilian careers. Approximately 20% of Northrop Grumman’s 100,000 employees self-identify as veterans, and more than 2,000 are reservists.

The Northrop Grumman SkillBridge Program is an approved SkillBridge Program under Dept. of Defense Instruction 1322.29. The program is an opportunity for service members preparing for civilian careers to gain valuable civilian work experience during their last 6 months of service, for up to 180 days. The SkillBridge Program is open to all ranks and experience levels. SkillBridge participants are not eligible for compensation from Northrop Grumman, as they continue to receive military compensation and benefits as active-duty service members.

Responsibilities for SkillBridge Program participation are:

Northrop Grumman Corporation (NGC) has developed the Northrop Grumman – SkillBridge Program (SkillBridge) utilizing the DoDI guidance for SkillBridge. The service member will be on the job training supporting a work schedule equivalent to 40hrs per week. Outlined below are the Goals, Objectives, and Outcomes for the program.

Goals – Provide separating service-members with job skills training in a professional setting during the final phase of their military service. This program is specifically designed to offer hands-on experience that result in the potential to convert to a full-time opportunity as the conclusion of the training. Participants will serve as a pipeline for high-speed, motivated military candidates into NGC.

Objectives - Service Members who complete the SkillBridge program will be highly trained, capable, future employees that align to the specific needs of the organization and are prepared to meet the NG mission “Defining Possible” on Day 1. This program provides comprehensive hands-on experience including professional development, networking with leadership, and training specifically focused on NG leadership principles, company history, customer/stakeholder engagement, product and service overview, and core job responsibilities.

Outcome – Offer service-members preparing for civilian careers a rewarding opportunity to join the Northrop Grumman team.

Job Description

Keysight Technologies has an exciting opportunity for an ASIC Design-for-Test (DFT) Engineer Intern within our ASIC R&D organization. This role provides hands-on experience across the semiconductor product development lifecycle, with a focus on Design-for-Test (DFT) methodologies used to ensure the manufacturability, quality, and reliability of advanced integrated circuits.

Working alongside experienced ASIC Test Engineers, you will gain exposure to industry-standard EDA tools and flows used for scan insertion, ATPG pattern generation, memory test, silicon validation, and production test development. This internship is an excellent opportunity for students interested in digital design, VLSI, semiconductor development, and hardware engineering to gain practical experience on real ASIC programs.

As an intern, you will collaborate with ASIC design, verification, physical design, and test engineers while contributing to projects that directly impact the successful development and release of next-generation semiconductor products.

This position is based in Colorado Springs, Colorado, consistently recognized as one of the nation's most desirable places to live.

Responsibilities

Responsibilities

- Support the development and verification of DFT architectures for complex digital and mixed-signal ASICs
- Learn and apply industry-standard DFT methodologies, including scan insertion, scan compression, ATPG, Streaming Scan Networks, and memory BIST (MBIST)
- Assist with ATPG pattern generation, coverage analysis, and debug using Siemens Tessent and other industry-standard EDA tools
- Develop scripts and automation solutions using Python, Ruby, Tcl, or similar languages to improve engineering workflows and data analysis
- Collaborate with ASIC design, verification, physical design, and product engineering teams to ensure testability requirements are incorporated throughout the design lifecycle
- Participate in silicon bring-up, characterization, debug, and failure analysis activities
- Analyze test results and help develop solutions to improve test quality, coverage, and efficiency

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications

- Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field
- Completion of sophomore year or higher by Summer 2027
- Coursework in Digital Logic Design, Computer Architecture, VLSI Design, FPGA Design, or related areas
- Understanding of digital circuits, finite state machines, and computer hardware fundamentals
- Programming or scripting experience in Python, C/C++, Tcl, Ruby, or similar languages
- Strong analytical, problem-solving, and debugging skills
- Demonstrated ability to work effectively in a collaborative team environment

Desired Qualifications

- Strong Interest in semiconductor design, ASIC development, hardware verification, or Design-for-Test (DFT) methodologies
- Familiarity with Verilog, SystemVerilog, or VHDL
- Knowledge of Linux/Unix environments and scripting
- Exposure to ASIC design flows, RTL development, simulation, or verification
- Familiarity with DFT concepts such as scan chains, ATPG, boundary scan, test compression, or memory BIST
- Exposure to EDA tools such as Siemens Tessent, Synopsys TestMAX, Cadence Modus, or similar tools
- Strong written and verbal communication skills
- Demonstrated ability to work independently while managing multiple technical tasks and priorities
